name: Notch Glide Rope Grab
title: Notch Glide Rope Grab: Uses, Fit and Buying Guide
meta: The Notch Glide rope grab gives tree climbers a compact way to grab a line for ascent, tending slack and rigging tasks. See uses, fit and safety notes.
tagline: A compact rope grab for climbers who want a clean bite on the line.
summary: The Notch Glide rope grab is a compact device that bites the rope in one direction and slides freely in the other, which makes it handy for ascent systems, tending slack and small rigging jobs. It is a tool for trained climbers who already understand how rope grabs load a line.
highlights: Grips in one direction, slides in the other
Useful in ascent and haul setups
Small enough to live on the saddle
Check rope diameter range before buying

body.h: Where a rope grab earns its spot
p: A rope grab is the piece you reach for when you need something to hold the line for you. On a stationary rope ascent it can act as the upper or foot-side grab, on the ground it can tend slack in a small haul, and in the tree it gives you a quick way to clip off to a line without tying another hitch.

The Notch Glide is built to run smoothly on the rope when you push it up and to lock when load comes on. That makes it quick to advance without fiddling, which matters when you are halfway up a long ascent and tired.

Rope grabs only work on the diameter and construction of rope they were designed for, so check the manufacturer's range against your climbing line before you commit to it. Watch the cam teeth and spring for wear, dirt and pitch, and retire the device if it slips, sticks or shows damage.

Life-support gear must meet ANSI Z133 requirements and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers. A rope grab is not a descent device and should never be your only point of attachment. Browse the full rope grab range to compare options.

faq.q: Can I use the Notch Glide as my only life-support connection?
faq.a: No. Use it as part of a system set up per the manufacturer's instructions, with a proper backup, and only after training.

faq.q: What rope does the Notch Glide fit?
faq.a: Check the rope diameter range in the Notch instructions and match it to your line before use.

name: Bandit Replacement Lanyard (Without Snap)
title: Bandit Replacement Lanyard Without Snap: Rope Only
meta: The Bandit replacement lanyard without snap lets you swap a worn positioning lanyard rope and keep your own adjuster and connector. Fit and care notes.
tagline: Fresh lanyard rope for climbers who already own the hardware.
summary: The Bandit replacement lanyard without snap is the rope only, for climbers who want to swap a worn positioning lanyard and keep their existing adjuster and carabiner or snap. You pay for the part that wears out instead of a whole new kit.
highlights: Replacement rope for a positioning lanyard
Supplied without a snap or carabiner
Keeps your existing adjuster in service
Lower cost than a full lanyard kit
Retire the old rope once it shows wear
specs: Use your own adjuster and connector

body.h: Why buy the rope on its own
p: Lanyard rope takes a beating. It gets dragged over bark, pinched in adjusters and nicked when you are cutting close. The hardware usually outlasts the rope by years, so a replacement lanyard without a snap is the sensible way to keep a familiar setup going.

Pair it with the adjuster you already trust and a connector rated for life support. Make sure the termination on the rope suits the connector you plan to use and that the connector closes and locks fully once it is on.

Thread the rope through your adjuster following the device maker's instructions, and tie a stopper knot in the tail so the adjuster cannot run off the end. Test the setup low to the ground before trusting it at height.

Life-support gear must meet ANSI Z133 requirements and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers. Retire the lanyard if you see cuts, glazing, core shots or stiff spots. More options are in our rope lanyards section.

faq.q: Does the Bandit replacement lanyard come with a snap?
faq.a: No. This version is rope only, so you need your own life-support rated snap or locking carabiner.

faq.q: Will it work with my mechanical adjuster?
faq.a: Check the rope diameter against your adjuster's approved range in its instructions before use.

name: Marlow Boa 9mm Prusik Cord
title: Marlow Boa 9mm Prusik Cord: Hitch Cord Guide
meta: Marlow Boa 9mm prusik cord is a hitch cord for tree climbers who tie their own friction hitches and eye-to-eyes. Sizing tips, care and safety notes.
tagline: A 9mm hitch cord for climbers who like to tune their own friction hitch.
summary: Marlow Boa prusik cord is a 9mm cord for tying friction hitches on arborist climbing lines. Buy it in the length you need to make up a Distel, Valdotain or similar hitch, then have eyes finished by a qualified splicer or use a tested termination.
highlights: Cut to the length you need
For Distel, Valdotain and similar hitches
Good match for mid-size climbing lines
Inspect often and replace when glazed

body.h: Matching hitch cord to your line
p: A friction hitch is only as good as the pairing between hitch cord and climbing line. A 9mm cord sits in the middle of the range, giving a balance of grip and smooth tending on most common arborist ropes. Thinner cord grabs harder, thicker cord runs smoother, so test your combination before you commit.
Buying by the foot lets you cut a hitch to suit how you climb. Many climbers make up a short eye-to-eye for MRS and a slightly longer piece for experimenting with wraps.
Eyes on a hitch cord carry your full weight, so use sewn or spliced eyes made by a qualified provider, or a properly dressed and tested knot taught in your training. Do not improvise.

Life-support gear must meet ANSI Z133 requirements and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers. Hitch cord wears faster than any other part of your system. Replace it when the cover glazes, fuzzes heavily or stiffens from heat. See more tech cordage.

faq.q: How much Marlow Boa cord do I need for a hitch?
faq.a: It depends on the hitch and how you terminate it. Measure an existing hitch you like and add a little for terminations.

faq.q: Is 9mm hitch cord right for my climbing line?
faq.a: It suits many mid-size arborist lines, but always test the pairing low to the ground and follow both manufacturers' guidance.

name: Yale XTC 12-Strand Arborist Rope
title: Yale XTC 12-Strand Arborist Rope: Climbing Line Guide
meta: Yale XTC 12-strand arborist rope is a classic hollow-braid style climbing line for tree work. Learn how it handles, how to inspect it and what to pair it with.
tagline: A traditional braid climbing line from Yale for working tree climbers.
summary: The Yale XTC 12-strand arborist rope is a climbing line from the XTC family built for tree work, with a braid that handles predictably with friction hitches and is easy to inspect. It suits climbers who want a no-surprises line for everyday MRS climbing.
highlights: Climbing line from Yale's XTC family
Easy to inspect along its length
Sold in hanks, check length at checkout

p: Twelve-strand rope has a simpler braid than the 16 and 24-strand lines that dominate today, and many climbers like how plainly it shows wear. Run your hands along it and abrasion, flat spots and stiffness show up quickly.

In the tree it pairs well with a traditional friction hitch on MRS. Before you trust any combination, test your hitch cord on the line low to the ground and adjust wraps until it grabs cleanly and tends without fighting you.
Keep your climbing line out of chips, oil and sun when it is not in use, and store it in a rope bag. Never cut near it or use it for rigging loads.

Life-support gear must meet ANSI Z133 requirements and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers. Retire the rope if you find cuts, glazing, chemical contact or a section that feels different from the rest. Compare more climbing rope options.

faq.q: Can I use Yale XTC 12-strand for rigging?
faq.a: No. Keep your climbing line for climbing only and use dedicated rigging rope for lowering loads.

faq.q: What hitch cord works with this rope?
faq.a: Most common arborist hitch cords work, but test your exact combination low to the ground before climbing on it.

name: Courant Komora Climbing Rope
title: Courant Komora Climbing Rope: 16-Strand Line Guide
meta: The Courant Komora climbing rope is a 16-strand arborist line for tree climbers on MRS and SRS. Learn how it handles, what to pair it with and how to inspect it.
tagline: A 16-strand arborist climbing line from Courant for everyday tree work.
summary: The Courant Komora climbing rope is a 16-strand arborist line made for tree climbing, with a firm cover that runs well through friction hitches and mechanical devices. It suits climbers who want a dependable everyday line from a European maker that builds only climbing and work rope.
highlights: Firm cover for hitches and devices
For MRS and, where approved, SRS
Sold in hanks, check length at checkout

p: Sixteen-strand ropes are the workhorse of modern tree climbing. A tight cover over a core gives a line that holds its shape, resists picking up bark and runs cleanly through a friction hitch or pulley.

If you plan to run the Komora on a mechanical device, check that the device maker lists the rope or its diameter and construction as compatible before you climb on it. Then test the setup low to the ground and adjust until it tends smoothly.

Keep your climbing line in a rope bag, away from chips, bar oil, fuel and long hours of sun. Never cut near it, and never use it to lower wood. A climbing line that has caught a rigging load is a rigging line from then on.

Life-support gear must meet ANSI Z133 requirements and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers. Retire the rope if you find cuts, glazing, chemical contact, core damage or a section that feels different from the rest. Compare more 16-strand climbing rope.

faq.q: Can I use the Courant Komora with a mechanical SRS device?
faq.a: Only if the device manufacturer approves that rope type and diameter. Check both sets of instructions first.

faq.q: How long should I buy?
faq.a: Pick a length that reaches the ground from your highest typical tie-in point doubled for MRS, plus a margin.

name: Samson ArborFreak Pine Beauty Climbing Rope
title: Samson ArborFreak Pine Beauty Climbing Rope Guide
h1: Samson ArborFreak Pine Beauty Climbing Rope
meta: Samson ArborFreak Pine Beauty is a green 11.7mm, 16-strand climbing rope for tree climbers on MRS and SRS. See how it handles, care tips and safety notes.
tagline: The green colorway of Samson's 11.7mm ArborFreak climbing line.
summary: Samson ArborFreak in Pine Beauty is the green colorway of Samson's 11.7mm, 16-strand arborist climbing line. It is built to run smoothly through hitches and mechanical devices and to hold up to daily use in the tree.
highlights: Runs well through hitches and devices
Firm cover that resists bark pickup
Sold in hanks, check length at checkout

p: At 11.7mm the ArborFreak fits the sweet spot for most hitch cords, rope wrenches and SRS devices built around half-inch class lines. The 16-strand cover gives a firm hand and keeps its round profile, so it feeds evenly through a hitch or a device.

The green Pine Beauty color is easy to tell apart from the rest of the gear on the truck, which helps on crews running several lines. Check your device maker's compatibility list before running it on SRS.

Keep your climbing line in a rope bag, away from chips, bar oil, fuel and long hours of sun. Never cut near it, and never use it to lower wood. A climbing line that has caught a rigging load is a rigging line from then on.

Life-support gear must meet ANSI Z133 requirements and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers. Retire the rope if you find cuts, glazing, chemical contact, core damage or a section that feels different from the rest. Compare more 16-strand climbing rope.

faq.q: What diameter is Samson ArborFreak?
faq.a: ArborFreak is an 11.7mm climbing line, which fits most hitch cords and many SRS devices designed for that range.

faq.q: Is Pine Beauty different from other ArborFreak colors?
faq.a: It is a colorway of the same rope. Pick the color that stands out on your jobs and in your truck.

name: Yale XTC 16 Fire Climbing Rope
title: Yale XTC 16 Fire Climbing Rope: Specs and Buying Guide
meta: Yale XTC Fire is a 1/2 in, 16-strand arborist climbing rope in a bright fire colorway. How it handles with hitches and devices, plus care and safety notes.
tagline: A half-inch 16-strand Yale climbing line in a bright, easy-to-spot colorway.
summary: Yale XTC Fire is a 1/2 in, 16-strand arborist climbing rope in a bright red and orange colorway that is easy to see in the canopy. It is a traditional all-round line for MRS climbing that also suits many devices built for half-inch rope.
highlights: Suited to MRS with common friction hitches
Firm braid that holds its shape
Sold in hanks, check length at checkout

p: The XTC line has been a standard on tree crews for a long time because it does what it is supposed to do. The 16-strand braid stays round, feeds evenly through a friction hitch and is easy to tie and untie.
The fire colorway stands out against foliage and bark, which makes it easier for the ground crew to track your line and keep chips and saws away from it.

Keep your climbing line in a rope bag, away from chips, bar oil, fuel and long hours of sun. Never cut near it, and never use it to lower wood. A climbing line that has caught a rigging load is a rigging line from then on.

Life-support gear must meet ANSI Z133 requirements and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers. Retire the rope if you find cuts, glazing, chemical contact, core damage or a section that feels different from the rest. Compare more 16-strand climbing rope.

faq.q: Is Yale XTC Fire good for SRS?
faq.a: It can be, if your SRS device maker approves half-inch 16-strand rope. Check the instructions before you climb on it.

faq.q: What hitch cord pairs with XTC Fire?
faq.a: Most 8 to 10mm hitch cords work. Test the combination low to the ground first.

name: Courant Rebel Yellow Climbing Rope
title: Courant Rebel Yellow Climbing Rope: Static Line Guide
meta: The Courant Rebel climbing rope in yellow is a static arborist line suited to SRS and MRS tree climbing. Learn how it handles, what to pair it with and care tips.
tagline: A static arborist climbing line from Courant in high-visibility yellow.
summary: The Courant Rebel climbing rope is a low-stretch arborist line that suits single rope technique as well as moving rope climbing. The yellow version is easy to pick out in the tree and on the ground.
highlights: Sold in hanks, check length at checkout

p: Static lines give less bounce on long SRS ascents, so more of each stroke turns into height. That is why low-stretch ropes like the Rebel have become common on crews that climb big trees on a single rope.
Before you run it in a mechanical device, confirm the device maker lists a compatible diameter and construction. Test the system low to the ground and set up a proper anchor and backup as trained.

Keep your climbing line in a rope bag, away from chips, bar oil, fuel and long hours of sun. Never cut near it, and never use it to lower wood. A climbing line that has caught a rigging load is a rigging line from then on.

Life-support gear must meet ANSI Z133 requirements and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers. Retire the rope if you find cuts, glazing, chemical contact, core damage or a section that feels different from the rest. Compare more static climbing rope.

faq.q: Is Courant Rebel good for SRS?
faq.a: It is a low-stretch line that many climbers use for SRS. Check your device's compatible rope list before use.

faq.q: Does the yellow color change performance?
faq.a: No. Color is for visibility and telling lines apart on the truck.

name: Samson 3/4 in Pro-Master Rigging Rope
title: Samson 3/4 Pro-Master Rigging Rope: Buying Guide
meta: Samson 3/4 in Pro-Master rigging rope is a heavy rigging line for lowering big wood with blocks and lowering devices. Use, inspection and safety notes.
tagline: A 3/4 in rigging line for crews lowering heavy wood.
summary: Samson 3/4 in Pro-Master rigging rope is a heavy rigging line for crews lowering big leads and wood with blocks, lowering devices and port-a-wraps. The thick diameter gives it more capacity and more to grip on the bollard than smaller lines.
highlights: For heavy lowering with blocks and devices
Stands up to repeated rigging cycles
Sold in hanks, check length at checkout

body.h: Where a 3/4 in rigging line fits
p: Most removal crews keep a 1/2 in or 5/8 in line for everyday pieces and a 3/4 in line for the heavy stuff: big tops, wide leads and trunk sections. The thicker rope gives more capacity and more surface on the lowering device, which helps the groundie control a heavy run.
Size the whole system together. Your block, sling, lowering device and anchor all need to handle the forces you are generating, not just the rope. Shock loads from letting wood free fall add up fast.
Check the rope after every job for cuts, glazing, crushed sections and heat damage from the bollard. Keep it out of the chipper path and away from saw chain.
Rigging should be planned by trained, qualified people following ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's working load guidance. Retire the line once it shows damage. See more rigging rope.

faq.q: When do I need 3/4 in rigging rope instead of 1/2 in?
faq.a: When the wood you are lowering and the forces involved exceed what your smaller line and hardware are rated for. Work it out with your crew lead before the cut.

faq.q: Can I splice Samson Pro-Master?
faq.a: Use a splice that Samson approves for that construction and have it done by someone trained in it.

name: Teufelberger 8mm Ocean Polyester Hitch Cord (By the Foot)
title: Ocean Polyester 8mm Hitch Cord by the Foot
h1: Teufelberger 8mm Ocean Polyester Hitch Cord (By the Foot)
meta: Ocean polyester 8mm hitch cord by the foot from Teufelberger, for tree climbers tying their own friction hitches and eye-to-eyes. Sizing, care and safety tips.
tagline: 8mm polyester hitch cord, cut to the length you need.
summary: Ocean polyester hitch cord in 8mm is a slim, grippy cord for tying friction hitches on arborist climbing lines. Buy it by the foot to make up a hitch, a short prusik or a spare to keep in the bag.
highlights: Slim diameter for a firm grab
Good for tuning your own hitch length

p: An 8mm cord grabs harder than thicker cords on the same climbing line, so it suits climbers on thinner ropes or anyone who likes a positive bite. On thick lines it can grab too hard and get grabby on descent, so test it before you commit.
Buying by the foot lets you cut exactly what your hitch needs. Measure a hitch you already like and add enough for terminations.
Eyes on a hitch cord carry your full weight. Have them sewn or spliced by a qualified provider, or use a knot taught and tested in your training. Do not improvise terminations at height.

Life-support gear must meet ANSI Z133 requirements and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers. Hitch cord is a consumable. Replace it when the cover glazes, fuzzes heavily or stiffens from heat. See more tech cordage.

faq.q: How much 8mm Ocean cord do I need for a Distel?
faq.a: Measure a hitch you like and add enough for your terminations. Many climbers start around 30 inches and adjust.

faq.q: Is 8mm too thin for my rope?
faq.a: It works best on thinner climbing lines. On larger ropes it may grab too hard, so test low to the ground.

name: Teufelberger 9.3mm Epicord Hitch Cord (By the Foot)
title: Teufelberger Epicord 9.3mm Hitch Cord by the Foot
h1: Teufelberger 9.3mm Epicord Hitch Cord (By the Foot)
meta: Teufelberger Epicord 9.3mm hitch cord by the foot is a popular choice for tree climbers tying friction hitches. Learn how it pairs, how to finish it and care tips.
tagline: The 9.3mm version of Teufelberger's popular Epicord hitch cord, sold by the foot.
summary: Teufelberger Epicord is one of the most widely used hitch cords in tree climbing, and the 9.3mm size gives a balance of grip and smooth tending on most mid-size arborist lines. Buy it by the foot and cut the hitch to fit how you climb.

p: Epicord earned its following by being predictable. In 9.3mm it sits in the middle of the hitch cord range, so it pairs well with most climbing lines in the 11 to 13mm class without locking up or slipping.
Cut what you need for a Distel, Valdotain or similar hitch, then add enough for terminations. Some climbers keep a spare length in the bag for a quick swap on long jobs.
Eyes on a hitch cord carry your full weight. Have them sewn or spliced by a qualified provider, or use a knot taught and tested in your training. Do not improvise terminations at height.

Life-support gear must meet ANSI Z133 requirements and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers. Hitch cord is a consumable. Replace it when the cover glazes, fuzzes heavily or stiffens from heat. See more tech cordage.

faq.q: Should I pick 8mm or 9.3mm Epicord?
faq.a: Thinner cord grabs harder, thicker cord tends more smoothly. Match it to your climbing line and test both if you can.

faq.q: Can I tie my own eyes in Epicord?
faq.a: Use sewn or spliced eyes from a qualified provider, or a termination knot you were trained on and have tested.

name: Yale 10mm Bee Line Hitch Cord (By the Foot)
title: Yale Bee Line 10mm Hitch Cord by the Foot
h1: Yale 10mm Bee Line Hitch Cord (By the Foot)
meta: Yale Bee Line 10mm hitch cord by the foot is a heat-tolerant friction hitch cord for tree climbers on larger ropes. How to size it, finish it and care for it.
tagline: 10mm Bee Line hitch cord from Yale, cut to the length you need.
summary: Yale Bee Line in 10mm is a hitch cord built to handle the heat a friction hitch makes on descent, sold by the foot so you can cut your own hitch. The thicker diameter suits climbers on larger lines who want smooth tending.

p: Bee Line has been a staple hitch cord for years, valued for how well its cover handles friction heat. At 10mm it tends smoothly and is less likely to lock up on thicker climbing lines than 8mm cord.
On thinner ropes a 10mm cord may need extra wraps to hold. Test the pairing low to the ground and adjust until it grabs and releases cleanly.
Eyes on a hitch cord carry your full weight. Have them sewn or spliced by a qualified provider, or use a knot taught and tested in your training. Do not improvise terminations at height.

Life-support gear must meet ANSI Z133 requirements and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers. Hitch cord is a consumable. Replace it when the cover glazes, fuzzes heavily or stiffens from heat. See more tech cordage.

faq.q: Is 10mm Bee Line too thick for my rope?
faq.a: It works best on larger climbing lines. On thin ropes it may need more wraps, so test it first.

faq.q: How long should I cut Bee Line for a hitch?
faq.a: Measure a hitch you like and add enough for terminations. Lengths vary with hitch style and rope.

name: 3M SecureFit Protective Eyewear, Gray Lens
title: 3M SecureFit Safety Glasses, Gray Lens: Fit and Uses
meta: 3M SecureFit safety glasses with a gray lens cut glare on bright jobs. A light, self-adjusting fit that stays put under helmets and muffs. Fit and care tips.
tagline: Light, self-adjusting 3M safety glasses with a gray lens for sunny jobs.
summary: 3M SecureFit safety glasses with a gray lens give tree crews light, comfortable eye protection that cuts glare on bright days. The temples flex to fit a wide range of head sizes, so they stay put while you climb, chip or drag brush.
highlights: Gray lens to cut glare in sun
Self-adjusting temples for a secure fit
Easy to stock for a whole crew

p: Sawdust, chips, twigs and chipper kickback are a constant on tree jobs. A pair of glasses you actually keep on all day protects you better than a face shield you flip up the moment it fogs.

The SecureFit temples apply gentle pressure that spreads around the head, so the glasses stay put when you look up into the canopy or bend over to feed the chipper. Gray lenses are for daylight work; switch to clear lenses in shade, early mornings and indoors.

Good safety glasses sit close to the face without pressing on your temples under a helmet strap or earmuff cushion. Try them with your helmet and hearing protection on, because that is how you will wear them all day.

Keep a spare pair in the truck so a scratched or lost pair never means working without eye protection. Rinse grit off with water before wiping the lenses, store them in a case or soft bag, and replace them once scratches start to blur your view. Look for the ANSI Z87.1 marking on the frame and lens when you need rated safety eyewear. Browse more eye protection.

faq.q: Can I wear gray-lens SecureFit glasses in low light?
faq.a: Gray lenses are meant for bright conditions. Use clear lenses in shade, at dusk or indoors.

faq.q: Do they fit under a helmet visor?
faq.a: Most users can wear them under a mesh or clear visor. Try them together before work.

name: Edge Brazeau Smoke Safety Glasses
title: Edge Brazeau Smoke Safety Glasses: Fit and Uses
meta: Edge Brazeau smoke safety glasses give tree crews glare-cutting eye protection with a sporty wraparound frame. Fit tips, care and when to use a smoke lens.
tagline: Sporty wraparound safety glasses with a smoke lens for bright days.
summary: Edge Brazeau smoke safety glasses are wraparound safety glasses with a dark lens for sunny jobs. They give tree workers sport-style looks with real eye protection for climbing, bucking and brush work.
highlights: Good spare pair for the truck

p: A smoke lens takes the edge off glare when you are looking up through the canopy or working in open sun. That cuts eye strain over a long day and helps you read the tree.
The wraparound frame helps keep chips and dust from coming in around the sides. Smoke lenses are for daylight; keep a clear pair handy for shade and low light.

Good safety glasses sit close to the face without pressing on your temples under a helmet strap or earmuff cushion. Try them with your helmet and hearing protection on, because that is how you will wear them all day.

Keep a spare pair in the truck so a scratched or lost pair never means working without eye protection. Rinse grit off with water before wiping the lenses, store them in a case or soft bag, and replace them once scratches start to blur your view. Look for the ANSI Z87.1 marking on the frame and lens when you need rated safety eyewear. Browse more eye protection.

faq.q: Are smoke lenses okay for climbing?
faq.a: They are good in bright sun. Under heavy shade or late in the day, a clear lens lets you see more.

faq.q: Do Brazeau glasses work with earmuffs?
faq.a: Most users find the temples sit fine under muff cushions. Try them with your setup first.

name: ERB Safety O.N.E. Ammo Safety Sunglasses

The Ammo has the look of a sport sunglass, which is part of the appeal: crew members are more likely to keep on a pair they like wearing.

Good safety glasses sit close to the face without pressing on your temples under a helmet strap or earmuff cushion. Try them with your helmet and hearing protection on, because that is how you will wear them all day.

faq.q: Can I wear the ERB Ammo in shade?
faq.a: Tinted lenses cut light, so use clear glasses in deep shade, at dusk or indoors.

name: ERB Safety O.N.E. Breakout Safety Sunglasses

h1: ERB Safety O.N.E. Breakout Safety Sunglasses
meta: ERB O.N.E. Breakout safety glasses pair sport-sunglass styling with eye protection for tree crews in bright sun. Fit tips, lens choice and care for the job.
tagline: ERB safety sunglasses with a sporty frame for bright days on the crew.

The Breakout's sporty frame is designed to be worn for a full shift. It is also inexpensive enough that losing a pair in the brush pile is not a big deal.

faq.q: How do I clean ERB Breakout lenses?

name: ERB Safety O.N.E. Free Ride (Metallic Frame) Safety Sunglasses
title: ERB O.N.E. Free Ride Metallic Safety Sunglasses

name: Kask Mesh Visor for Super Plasma Helmets
title: Kask Super Plasma Mesh Visor: Fit and Uses
h1: Kask Mesh Visor for Super Plasma Helmets
meta: The Kask mesh visor for Super Plasma helmets keeps chips and sawdust off your face while staying cool and fog-free. Fit, care and buying notes for tree crews.
tagline: A mesh face visor made to clip onto Kask Super Plasma helmets.
summary: The Kask mesh visor for Super Plasma helmets is a face screen that keeps chips, sawdust and twigs off your face without fogging the way a clear shield can. It is made to mount on Kask Super Plasma helmets and pairs with Kask earmuffs.
highlights: Mesh visor for Kask Super Plasma helmets

body.h: Why climbers run a mesh visor
p: Mesh is the default for most tree climbers because it breathes. Air moves through it, so it stays clear on hot days and when you are breathing hard on an ascent, while still stopping most chips and debris from the saw.
On the ground it is just as useful for limbing, bucking and feeding the chipper, where wood bits fly at face height.
The visor mounts to the Super Plasma using Kask's attachment system. Make sure it clicks in securely on both sides and flips up and down smoothly before you leave the ground.

Rinse sap and dust off with water and mild soap, let it dry, and replace it once it is bent, torn or hard to see through. A visor adds protection from chips and debris but does not replace safety glasses, so wear both. More options are in our eye protection range.

faq.q: Will this visor fit a Kask Zenith?
faq.a: No. It is made for the Super Plasma. Kask makes a separate visor for the Zenith.

faq.q: Do I still need safety glasses with a mesh visor?
faq.a: Yes. Mesh stops chips but not fine dust or splinters, so wear safety glasses underneath.

body.h: Why choose a plastic mesh visor
p: Plastic mesh is light and does not dent or rust the way some metal screens can. It breathes well, so it stays clear on hot days and when you are working hard in the tree.
It is a good fit for climbers who want face protection that weighs almost nothing and stays out of the way when flipped up.
The Zenith needs Kask's visor adaptors to take a visor. Check that you have them, then make sure the visor clicks in on both sides and pivots smoothly before you climb.

Rinse sap and dust off with water and mild soap, let it dry, and replace it once it is bent, torn or hard to see through. A visor adds protection from chips and debris but does not replace safety glasses, so wear both. More options are in our eye protection range.

faq.q: Do I need adaptors to fit this visor to my Zenith?
faq.a: Yes. The Zenith uses Kask visor adaptors to mount visors and earmuffs.

faq.q: Is plastic mesh as protective as metal mesh?
faq.a: Both screen chips and debris. Neither replaces safety glasses, so wear glasses underneath.

name: Kask Zenith Visor Adaptors
title: Kask Zenith Visor Adaptors: Mount Visors and Muffs
meta: Kask Zenith visor adaptors let you mount a Kask visor and earmuffs on your Zenith helmet. What they do, how to fit them and what to check before you climb.
tagline: The side adaptors that let a Kask Zenith take a visor and earmuffs.

highlights: Side mounts for Kask Zenith helmets
Allow a visor to be fitted

p: The Zenith is a popular lightweight helmet, but out of the box it is set up for climbing rather than saw work. The adaptors fit to the sides of the shell and give you mounting points for a Kask visor and earmuffs.
That turns the Zenith into a full saw helmet setup, so you can wear one helmet for climbing, rigging and running the saw.
Fit the adaptors following Kask's instructions, then attach your visor and muffs and check that each one locks in place and moves smoothly. Replace adaptors that are cracked, loose or worn.

Rinse sap and dust off with water and mild soap, let it dry, and replace it once it is bent, torn or hard to see through. A visor adds protection from chips and debris but does not replace safety glasses, so wear both. More options are in our eye protection range.

faq.q: Do the adaptors come with a visor?
faq.a: No. They are the mounting parts only. Buy a Zenith-compatible Kask visor separately.

faq.q: Will they fit a Super Plasma?
faq.a: No. They are made for the Zenith. The Super Plasma has its own mounting system.

name: First Aid Kit
title: Arborist First Aid Kit for Tree Crews and Trucks
meta: A first aid kit for tree crews to keep in the truck or on the job site. What to look for, how to stock it for saw cuts and splinters, and why training matters.
tagline: A jobsite first aid kit for the truck, chipper or gear bag.
summary: An arborist first aid kit puts basic wound care within reach on every tree job, from saw nicks and splinters to scrapes and bee stings. Keep one in each truck and know where it is before anyone starts a saw.
highlights: Basic wound care supplies in one case
Sized for a truck or gear bag
Covers common cuts, scrapes and splinters
Easy to restock as you use it
Pair with first aid and CPR training
specs: Check listing for the full list

body.h: What a tree crew needs on hand
p: Tree work brings a steady run of small injuries: saw nicks, splinters, rope burns, scrapes from bark and stings from wasps in a hollow limb. A stocked first aid kit means those get cleaned and covered right away instead of after the job.

Keep the kit in the same place on every truck so anyone on the crew can grab it without thinking. Many crews add a tourniquet, extra trauma dressings and any personal medications crew members need, such as for allergic reactions.

A kit is only as good as the person using it. ANSI Z133 expects crews to have people trained in first aid and CPR, and serious chainsaw injuries need a call to emergency services first. Build an emergency plan that covers your site address and how responders will reach a climber.
Check the kit monthly, restock what was used and swap out anything expired or water damaged. See more in our first aid section.

faq.q: Is a basic first aid kit enough for chainsaw injuries?
faq.a: It handles small cuts. For serious bleeding, call emergency services and use a tourniquet and trauma dressings as trained.

faq.q: How often should I check the kit?
faq.a: Check it monthly and after every use, and replace expired or used items.

name: Petzl JAG System Haul Kit
title: Petzl JAG System Haul Kit: Uses and Buying Guide
meta: The Petzl JAG System is a ready-to-use haul kit with pulleys and rope for mechanical advantage in rescue and rigging. Uses, setup notes and safety reminders.
tagline: A preassembled pulley haul kit for rescue and mechanical advantage.
summary: The Petzl JAG System is a ready-to-use haul kit that combines pulleys and rope to give you mechanical advantage for lifting and moving loads. Tree crews keep one for aerial rescue and for tensioning or hauling jobs.
highlights: Fast to deploy from its bag
For trained rescue and rigging use

body.h: Why crews carry a haul kit
p: When a climber is hurt or stuck in the tree, the ground crew needs to move fast. A preassembled haul kit like the JAG System means there is no building a pulley system from loose parts under stress. You clip it in and it is ready to pull.

The same kit earns its spot on regular jobs, too, for tensioning a line, pulling a lead over or lifting a piece that is too heavy to handle by hand. Petzl offers it in several lengths, so pick the reach that matches your setups.

Aerial rescue and mechanical advantage systems multiply forces, so they belong in trained hands. Practice rescues regularly so everyone on the crew knows the kit before they need it. Follow Petzl's instructions and ANSI Z133 for rescue planning.
Inspect pulleys, connectors and rope before each use and after any heavy load. Retire parts that are worn, cracked or damaged. More rescue gear is in our first aid and rescue section.

faq.q: What mechanical advantage does the JAG System give?
faq.a: It is a multi-pulley haul kit. Check Petzl's instructions for the ratio of the version you choose.

faq.q: Can I use it for rigging logs?
faq.a: Use it within Petzl's ratings and instructions. It is built for hauling and rescue, not for catching dynamic rigging loads.

name: Husqvarna Technical Saw Protection Glove
title: Husqvarna Technical Saw Protection Gloves Guide
meta: Husqvarna Technical saw protection gloves add chainsaw protection to the back of the left hand with good grip and feel. Sizing, fit and care tips for crews.
tagline: Chainsaw gloves with saw protection on the left hand and good dexterity.
summary: Husqvarna Technical saw protection gloves put cut-resistant protection on the back of the left hand, where chain contact most often happens, while keeping enough feel to run a saw and handle gear. They suit climbers and ground crews who cut all day.
highlights: Saw protection on the back of the left hand
Good grip and feel for saw work
Pair with chaps or saw pants

body.h: Why saw protection on the left hand
p: Your left hand is on the front handle and closest to the chain when a saw kicks back. Saw protection gloves put cut-resistant fibers on the back of that hand, which can slow or stop the chain long enough to reduce injury.
The Technical line is built for feel as well as protection, so you can still work the chain brake, grab rope and handle small hardware without pulling the gloves off.

Gloves should fit snugly without bunching at the fingertips. Too loose and they catch, too tight and your hands tire fast. Wash them as the label directs and keep them away from fuel and bar oil when you can.

Saw protection reduces injury but does not make you cut-proof. Use them with chaps or saw pants, a helmet, eye and hearing protection, and good saw handling as trained. Retire gloves with cuts through the protective layer. See more work gloves.

faq.q: Do these gloves protect both hands?
faq.a: Saw protection is on the back of the left hand. Check the listing and label for details.

faq.q: How do I size Husqvarna gloves?
faq.a: Measure around your palm and check Husqvarna's size chart. A snug fit gives the best feel on the saw.

name: 3M Corded Earplugs with Carry Case
title: 3M Corded Earplugs with Carry Case: Fit and Uses
meta: 3M corded earplugs with a carry case give tree crews reusable hearing protection that stays clean in the truck. Fit, care tips and when to pair them with muffs.
tagline: Corded earplugs in a case, ready for saw, chipper and grinder work.
summary: 3M corded earplugs with a carry case give tree workers simple hearing protection that stays clean between uses. The cord keeps them around your neck when you pull them out, and the case keeps grit off them in the truck.
highlights: Corded so they hang around your neck
Light and easy to wear all day
Works under a helmet or with muffs

body.h: Hearing protection for every crew member
p: Chainsaws, chippers, stump grinders and blowers all run loud enough to damage hearing over a career. Earplugs are the simplest way to protect everyone, especially groundies who move between machines all day.
The cord means you can pull the plugs out to talk with the crew and let them hang without losing them in the brush. When the chipper starts up again, they go straight back in.

Earplugs only work if they are fitted right. Follow the fitting instructions on the package and check the seal; the noise should sound noticeably muffled. Many crews double up with earmuffs around the chipper and grinder.
Keep them in the case, wash reusable plugs with mild soap and water and replace them when they get hard, torn or dirty. Check the package for the noise reduction rating. See more hearing protection.

faq.q: Are these earplugs reusable?
faq.a: Check the package. Reusable plugs can be washed; foam plugs are generally meant for limited use.

faq.q: Can I wear earplugs and earmuffs together?
faq.a: Yes. Many crews double up around chippers and grinders for extra protection.
